pathway.title: Beazer Homes Usa Inc — Full credit assessment
pathway.question: Should we own this issuer, in which instrument, and why?

runs.text: Earnings, not the debt schedule, is the central credit problem. Revenue for the first nine months of fiscal 2026 fell 18.36% as closings dropped 22.1%, and homebuilding gross margin before impairments, abandonments and interest slid to 15.6% from 18.3%, while general and administrative costs did not fall, so the company moved from an operating profit to an operating loss. The issuer's EBITDA also adds back interest amortized to cost of sales; on operating income plus depreciation and amortization the twelve months to June 30, 2026 are negative and leverage on that basis is not calculable. Interest is therefore being paid from liquidity and borrowing, not from earnings. Basis: calculation C6; Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-06-30_issuer_bzh-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 40; 10-Q_2026-06-30_issuer_bzh-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 44

Liquidity is adequate for now but thin against the pace of cash use. Operating cash outflow plus capital expenditures over nine months was large because inventory was built ahead of closings, the revolver went from undrawn at fiscal 2025 year end to a 73.49% utilisation including letters of credit, and cash plus undrawn capacity covers only 0.67x of the nine-month outflow. Seasonality and backlog conversion could reverse part of this, but the covenant levels that govern revolver access are not printed, so headroom is not established. Net debt to EBITDA of 23.10x and cover of 0.63x are on the issuer's EBITDA; pro forma for the August 6, 2026 merger they are not established. Basis: calculation C7; calculation C4; Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-06-30_issuer_bzh-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 17; 10-Q_2026-06-30_issuer_bzh-20260630.htm.jsonl, pages 55–56

Refinancing risk is low until the end of the decade and market access remains open at a higher price. The remaining 2027 notes were redeemed with the proceeds of $400.0 million of 2032 notes sold at par in June 2026, and the nearest maturity is now the 2029 notes in October 2029, with the revolver terminating in March 2030. The new notes carry a higher coupon than the notes they replaced and S&P lowered its rating to B- with a negative outlook, while Moody's kept B2 and a stable outlook, so access is open but increasingly expensive. Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-K_2025-09-30_issuer_bzh-20250930.htm.jsonl, page 91; 10-Q_2026-06-30_issuer_bzh-20260630.htm.jsonl, pages 18–19; 10-Q_2026-06-30_issuer_bzh-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 57

The asset base is the main support but it is a recovery question for another module. Inventory is 1.68x total debt at carrying value and 60.0% of active lots are held under options, which limits owned land, yet inventory includes capitalized interest and land held for sale, and the value of that inventory in a downturn, and the ranking and guarantee terms that decide who is paid from it, are not assessed here. Basis: calculation C5; 10-Q_2026-06-30_issuer_bzh-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 9; 10-Q_2026-06-30_issuer_bzh-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 58

Financial policy is at odds with the stated deleveraging goal. The company repurchased $66.2 million of stock in nine months while net debt rose, and net debt to net capitalization is 52.8% against a goal of the low 30% range by the end of fiscal 2027. The pending cash acquisition at $33.50 per share changes who sets financial policy after closing, and nothing in the filings says how the notes would be treated. Basis: 10-K_2025-09-30_issuer_bzh-20250930.htm.jsonl, page 8; 10-Q_2026-06-30_issuer_bzh-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 41; 10-Q_2026-06-30_issuer_bzh-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 33; 10-Q_2026-06-30_issuer_bzh-20260630.htm.jsonl, pages 57–58; Business & governance (CP-1A)

runs.text: Strengths: the company has no debt maturing before October 2029, its notes and revolver are unsecured and guaranteed by substantially all significant subsidiaries, it carries no mortgage-subsidiary debt, inventory exceeds total debt, and its option-based land model limits owned land. Audited statements, effective internal control and an extended revolver add to transparency and flexibility. Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-Q_2026-06-30_issuer_bzh-20260630.htm.jsonl, pages 17–18; 10-Q_2026-06-30_issuer_bzh-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 58

Weaknesses: earnings have turned to an operating loss, leverage on the issuer's own EBITDA has risen from 5.86x to 23.10x and cash interest cover is 0.63x, cash flow is negative while inventory grows, the revolver is heavily used, shareholder returns have continued, and the company faces a change of control whose debt treatment is not stated. Pro forma net debt and leverage for the merger are not established. Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-Q_2026-06-30_issuer_bzh-20260630.htm.jsonl, pages 3–4; 10-Q_2026-06-30_issuer_bzh-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 41

blocks.title: Transaction summary and new debt issues

runs.text: On August 6, 2026 the company agreed to be acquired by Dream Finders Homes, Inc. for $33.50 per share in cash. A Dream Finders subsidiary would merge into the company, which would survive as a wholly owned subsidiary and stop being publicly traded. Closing is expected in the fourth quarter of calendar 2026 and needs stockholder approval, regulatory approval and other customary conditions. The agreement restricts the company to ordinary-course operations in the interim, which the company says will not prevent it from meeting debt service, and the risk list notes a possible termination fee without stating an amount. Basis: 10-Q_2026-06-30_issuer_bzh-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 33; 10-Q_2026-06-30_issuer_bzh-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 34

In June 2026 the company sold $400.0 million of 8.000% Senior Notes due 2032 at par in a private placement to qualified institutional buyers, with the first semiannual interest payment due in January 2027, and used the proceeds to redeem the remaining $357.3 million of its 5.875% Senior Notes due 2027, recording a $0.7 million loss on extinguishment. This extends the nearest note maturity from October 2027 to October 2029 and adds a longer, higher-coupon tranche. Basis: 10-Q_2026-06-30_issuer_bzh-20260630.htm.jsonl, pages 15–16; 10-Q_2026-06-30_issuer_bzh-20260630.htm.jsonl, pages 18–19; 10-Q_2026-06-30_issuer_bzh-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 61

In March 2026 the company raised its unsecured revolving facility commitment from $365.0 million to $525.0 million, including up to $100.0 million for letters of credit, and extended the termination date from March 15, 2028 to March 13, 2030. It may request a further increase of up to $100.0 million for a maximum of $625.0 million. At June 30, 2026 it had $340.0 million drawn and $45.8 million of letters of credit, leaving $139.2 million of remaining capacity. Basis: 10-Q_2026-06-30_issuer_bzh-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 17; 10-Q_2026-03-31_issuer_bzh-20260331.htm.jsonl, page 60

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Beazer is a land-light US homebuilder facing a change of control: Dream Finders Homes agreed on August 6, 2026 to buy it for $33.50 per share in cash, and the supplied filings do not say how the notes or revolver are treated at closing.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The operating model spans 13 states and three segments with no mortgage subsidiary, but nine-month revenue fell with closings while the company kept repurchasing shares as net debt rose. Governance disclosure is orderly, yet post-closing financial policy cannot be assessed from these sources.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The pending acquisition is the dominant fact for creditors, and its terms are only partly known. Dream Finders would pay $33.50 per share in cash, the company would survive as its wholly owned subsidiary, closing is expected in the fourth quarter of calendar 2026 and stockholder and regulatory approval are still required. The company says the interim operating restrictions will not stop it meeting debt service, but the filings give no termination fee amount, no financing plan and no treatment of the notes or revolver on a change of control, so the effect on bondholders is not established.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The revenue base is spread across 13 states but leans on the West. West produced 62.25% of fiscal 2025 revenue and 57.98% of nine-month fiscal 2026 revenue, against 63.43% in the prior nine months, so the mix is moving toward the Southeast, which rose to 17.82% from 12.52%. Net new orders fell over the nine months while the average price in backlog rose, which supports revenue only if closings recover.

fields.value: The land-light strategy limits balance-sheet land risk but carries a large contingent commitment. The company controlled 60.0% of its active lots through option agreements, with deposits and pre-acquisition costs of $387.4 million at risk and a remaining purchase price of $1.63 billion that it expects mostly to exercise, so a demand shortfall would hit liquidity through forfeited deposits or cash spent exercising options.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Capital allocation has favoured shareholders while leverage rose. The board approved a $100.0 million repurchase program in April 2025 and the company has bought back $78.7 million since, including $66.2 million in the first nine months of fiscal 2026, paying no dividends. Its stated goal is a net debt to net capitalization ratio in the low 30% range by the end of fiscal 2027, against 52.8% at June 30, 2026 and 39.5% at fiscal 2025 year end.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Governance disclosure is orderly but incomplete. One person is Chairman, President and Chief Executive Officer, the auditor gave unqualified opinions on the statements and internal control for fiscal 2025, and a rights agreement protects tax assets, yet board independence, executive pay and large holders sit in a proxy statement that is not supplied. The company has no mortgage subsidiary, which keeps finance-company debt out of the perimeter.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The strongest evidence against reading the change of control as a creditor risk is that the company refinanced and extended before the announcement: it issued $400.0 million of notes at par in June 2026, redeemed the remaining $357.3 million of its 2027 notes, and lifted its revolver commitment to $525.0 million with a March 2030 termination date. Moody's reaffirmed a stable outlook in June 2026, and the company states the merger restrictions will not impair debt service. The view would change toward comfort if the indentures show a change-of-control repurchase right at par or above, or if the acquirer's financing plan leaves the notes outstanding with a stronger parent. It would change toward concern if closing needs the notes or revolver to be amended, if S&P, whose outlook is negative, downgrades again, or if repurchases continue while net debt keeps rising.

fields.value: On August 6, 2026 the company agreed to be acquired by Dream Finders Homes, Inc. for $33.50 per share in cash. A Dream Finders subsidiary would merge into the company, which would survive as a wholly owned subsidiary and stop being publicly traded. Closing is expected in the fourth quarter of calendar 2026 and needs stockholder approval, regulatory approval and other customary conditions. The agreement restricts the company to ordinary-course operations in the interim, which the company says will not prevent it from meeting debt service, and the risk list notes a possible termination fee without stating an amount.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: In June 2026 the company sold $400.0 million of 8.000% Senior Notes due 2032 at par in a private placement to qualified institutional buyers, with the first semiannual interest payment due in January 2027, and used the proceeds to redeem the remaining $357.3 million of its 5.875% Senior Notes due 2027, recording a $0.7 million loss on extinguishment. This extends the nearest note maturity from October 2027 to October 2029 and adds a longer, higher-coupon tranche.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: In March 2026 the company raised its unsecured revolving facility commitment from $365.0 million to $525.0 million, including up to $100.0 million for letters of credit, and extended the termination date from March 15, 2028 to March 13, 2030. It may request a further increase of up to $100.0 million for a maximum of $625.0 million. At June 30, 2026 it had $340.0 million drawn and $45.8 million of letters of credit, leaving $139.2 million of remaining capacity.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Fundamental credit synthesis for Beazer Homes Usa Inc (issuer-915840) as of 2026-11-18 on the Full credit assessment pathway (credit_snapshot). Scope: the credit profile of the consolidated registrant from the Financial foundation, Business & governance and Source readiness findings and the five supplied filings. It assigns no rating and makes no security, legal-capacity or portfolio conclusion.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Beazer's fundamental credit profile is weak and deteriorating: earnings have fallen below the level that supports its debt, with net debt to EBITDA at 23.10x for the twelve months to June 30, 2026 against 5.86x at FY2025 and EBITDA covering cash interest only 0.63x.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Support comes from a maturity profile with no debt due before October 2029, an unsecured structure, an inventory base that exceeds total debt, and a pending all-cash acquisition whose effect on the notes is not established. The primary downside is continued cash burn: nine months of inventory growth left free cash flow negative and liquidity covers only 0.67x of that outflow. The pro forma effect of the August 6, 2026 merger on net debt and leverage is not established.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation C4; calculation C1; Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A)

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Earnings, not the debt schedule, is the central credit problem. Revenue for the first nine months of fiscal 2026 fell 18.36% as closings dropped 22.1%, and homebuilding gross margin before impairments, abandonments and interest slid to 15.6% from 18.3%, while general and administrative costs did not fall, so the company moved from an operating profit to an operating loss. The issuer's EBITDA also adds back interest amortized to cost of sales; on operating income plus depreciation and amortization the twelve months to June 30, 2026 are negative and leverage on that basis is not calculable. Interest is therefore being paid from liquidity and borrowing, not from earnings.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation C6; Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-06-30_issuer_bzh-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 40; 10-Q_2026-06-30_issuer_bzh-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 44

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Liquidity is adequate for now but thin against the pace of cash use. Operating cash outflow plus capital expenditures over nine months was large because inventory was built ahead of closings, the revolver went from undrawn at fiscal 2025 year end to a 73.49% utilisation including letters of credit, and cash plus undrawn capacity covers only 0.67x of the nine-month outflow. Seasonality and backlog conversion could reverse part of this, but the covenant levels that govern revolver access are not printed, so headroom is not established. Net debt to EBITDA of 23.10x and cover of 0.63x are on the issuer's EBITDA; pro forma for the August 6, 2026 merger they are not established.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Refinancing risk is low until the end of the decade and market access remains open at a higher price. The remaining 2027 notes were redeemed with the proceeds of $400.0 million of 2032 notes sold at par in June 2026, and the nearest maturity is now the 2029 notes in October 2029, with the revolver terminating in March 2030. The new notes carry a higher coupon than the notes they replaced and S&P lowered its rating to B- with a negative outlook, while Moody's kept B2 and a stable outlook, so access is open but increasingly expensive.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The asset base is the main support but it is a recovery question for another module. Inventory is 1.68x total debt at carrying value and 60.0% of active lots are held under options, which limits owned land, yet inventory includes capitalized interest and land held for sale, and the value of that inventory in a downturn, and the ranking and guarantee terms that decide who is paid from it, are not assessed here.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Financial policy is at odds with the stated deleveraging goal. The company repurchased $66.2 million of stock in nine months while net debt rose, and net debt to net capitalization is 52.8% against a goal of the low 30% range by the end of fiscal 2027. The pending cash acquisition at $33.50 per share changes who sets financial policy after closing, and nothing in the filings says how the notes would be treated.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The strongest case against a deteriorating view is that the decline looks cyclical and affordability-driven rather than structural. Net new orders rose 4.5% in the third quarter, the cancellation rate fell to 15.9% from 19.8%, backlog value rose 2.2% and the average price in backlog is higher, while the company attributes soft demand to mortgage rates near 52-week highs and consumer sentiment near all-time lows. The company also pushed out its maturities and enlarged its revolver before the acquisition was announced. The view would soften if quarterly closings recover and operating cash flow turns positive as inventory converts, if the revolver is repaid, or if the acquirer's financing leaves the notes with a stronger parent. It would worsen if closings and margins keep falling, if the revolver is drawn further, if covenant levels prove tight, or if repurchases continue.
